name: State Bank of Pakistan, Islamabad
assumptions: The dossier footprint covers only the domed part of a longer range; the satellite shows the block carrying on to the south-east and the office tower is a separate building, so neither is modelled here.
Wall height 11 m is an estimate from the street photo, using the car roof as the horizon and a 4 m bay, not a published figure.
Dome apex 20.4 m and collar height are fitted to the photos with the satellite dome diameter of about 29 m.
The dome centre was taken from a leaning satellite image and corrected by eye, so it may be off by a metre or two.
The south-west street front is inferred from the road, forecourt and fountain in the satellite and the Margalla hills on the left of the photo.
North-west and north-east faces repeat the slit rhythm of the street front; no photo shows them head on.
The south-east face is a plain wall because the real building continues there.
The ground-floor row of the central block is hidden behind the gate in every photo and is a plain glazed row.
The porch is read only from a pale slab in the satellite; its height and two-post support are guesses.
The dark south-east roof strip is drawn flush with the deck; whether it is a lower roof or a dark covering is unknown.
The dark and white honeycomb cells on the dome follow the recent street photo in layout, with about 10 dark rows on a white cap; the 1970 photos show it plain white.
Rooftop water tanks and the sentry posts seen in the street photo are left out as temporary or security items.
